KbArticles.Title: Remediation guidance for sse kms not used

Trait.Title: The S3 bucket is not encrypted at-rest with AWS KMS keys

Context.ProblemStatement: The S3 bucket uses SSE-S3 (Amazon S3-managed keys) or has no default encryption configured, instead of SSE-KMS (AWS Key Management Service keys). While SSE-S3 encrypts data at rest, it lacks the granular access control, key rotation management, and audit logging provided by KMS. With SSE-KMS, every decrypt operation generates a CloudTrail event, KMS key policies control which principals can decrypt objects, and customer managed keys (CMKs) provide full control over key lifecycle. The remediation configures SSE-KMS as the default encryption for the bucket, applying to all new objects uploaded without explicit encryption headers.
Context.RiskAssessment: Medium execution risk. Changing the default encryption only affects newly uploaded objects — existing objects retain their current encryption and remain accessible. However, applications writing to or reading from the bucket must have kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey permissions on the KMS key. Applications with only S3 permissions will fail to upload (missing kms:GenerateDataKey) or download (missing kms:Decrypt) new objects. Cross-account access becomes more complex — both the bucket policy AND KMS key policy must grant access. Blast radius: all applications writing new objects to this bucket. Fully reversible — default encryption can be changed back to SSE-S3 with a single API call. Existing objects are never re-encrypted by this change.
Context.AffectedScope: Single S3 bucket's default encryption configuration. Fix takes effect immediately for new objects — objects uploaded after the change use SSE-KMS. Not affected: existing objects (retain their current encryption), bucket policy, ACLs, versioning, lifecycle rules, Block Public Access, or any other bucket setting. Objects uploaded with an explicit x-amz-server-side-encryption header override the default. To re-encrypt existing objects, a separate S3 Batch Operations job is required.
Prerequisites: Bucket must exist and be accessible
A KMS key must exist (either AWS managed key 'aws/s3' or a customer managed key) — if using a CMK, it must be in the same region as the bucket
All applications writing to this bucket must have kms:GenerateDataKey permission on the chosen KMS key
All applications reading objects from this bucket must have kms:Decrypt permission on the chosen KMS key
For cross-account access: the KMS key policy must explicitly allow external accounts to use the key
Executing identity needs: s3:GetBucketEncryption, s3:PutBucketEncryption, kms:DescribeKey (to verify key exists)

Parameters.Name: KmsKeyId
Parameters.Description: KMS key ID, ARN, alias, or alias ARN for encryption. Use 'aws/s3' for the AWS managed key, or a CMK ARN for customer managed key. If not provided, defaults to the AWS managed 'aws/s3' key.

Parameters.Name: BucketKeyEnabled
Parameters.Description: Whether to enable S3 Bucket Keys to reduce KMS API costs. Default: true (recommended). Bucket Keys reduce KMS request costs by up to 99% by using a bucket-level key for a time-limited period.

Steps.Description: Capture current bucket encryption configuration for pre-check, rollback, and verification
Steps.Logic: 1. GetBucketEncryption(Bucket=amzn-s3-demo-bucket): capture the ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration. Store as snapshot.EncryptionConfig. If ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError, record as null (no default encryption configured — this is valid for older buckets). Note: since January 2023, all new S3 buckets have SSE-S3 encryption by default. 2. From the configuration, extract: current SSEAlgorithm (AES256 for SSE-S3, aws:kms for SSE-KMS, aws:kms:dsse for DSSE-KMS), current KMSMasterKeyID (if KMS), current BucketKeyEnabled. Store these as snapshot.CurrentAlgorithm, snapshot.CurrentKeyId, snapshot.CurrentBucketKey. 3. If ${KmsKeyId} is provided and is not 'aws/s3': call kms:DescribeKey(KeyId=${KmsKeyId}) to verify the key exists and is enabled. If NotFoundException or DisabledException, abort — key does not exist or is disabled. Store key ARN as snapshot.TargetKeyArn. 4. If NoSuchBucket error on any call, abort.

Steps.Description: Configure SSE-KMS as the default encryption for the bucket with optional Bucket Keys
Steps.Logic: Pre-check: if snapshot.CurrentAlgorithm == 'aws:kms' and snapshot.CurrentKeyId matches ${KmsKeyId} (or both are the AWS managed key), SKIP — already compliant. Determine the KMS key to use: if ${KmsKeyId} is provided, use it; otherwise omit KMSMasterKeyID to use the AWS managed 'aws/s3' key (when omitting KMSMasterKeyID with aws:kms algorithm, S3 uses the aws/s3 managed key). Determine BucketKeyEnabled: if ${BucketKeyEnabled} is provided, use it; otherwise default to true. Call PutBucketEncryption(Bucket=amzn-s3-demo-bucket, ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration={Rules:[{ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:{SSEAlgorithm:'aws:kms', KMSMasterKeyID:${KmsKeyId or omit}}, BucketKeyEnabled:${BucketKeyEnabled or true}}]}). Error handling: (a) NoSuchBucket — abort, bucket was deleted. (b) AccessDenied — executing identity lacks s3:PutBucketEncryption. (c) InvalidArgument with 'KMS key does not exist' — the specified key ID is invalid or in wrong region. (d) Throttling — exponential backoff, max 3 retries. Do NOT modify any other bucket settings. This change affects only new objects — existing objects retain their encryption.
Steps.Inverse: If snapshot.EncryptionConfig was null: call DeleteBucketEncryption(Bucket=amzn-s3-demo-bucket). Otherwise: PutBucketEncryption(Bucket=amzn-s3-demo-bucket, ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration=snapshot.EncryptionConfig). Note: reverting to SSE-S3 is a security regression that loses KMS audit logging and key policy controls for new objects.
Steps.VerifyAfter: GetBucketEncryption(Bucket=amzn-s3-demo-bucket): assert SSEAlgorithm is 'aws:kms' and KMSMasterKeyID matches the configured key.

Steps.Description: Confirm SSE-KMS is configured as default encryption and Bucket Keys are enabled
Steps.Logic: 1. GetBucketEncryption(Bucket=amzn-s3-demo-bucket): read current configuration. 2. Assert Rules[0].ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault.SSEAlgorithm == 'aws:kms'. 3. If a specific ${KmsKeyId} was provided: assert Rules[0].ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault.KMSMasterKeyID matches the expected key ARN. Note: S3 normalizes key IDs to full ARNs. 4. Assert Rules[0].BucketKeyEnabled == expected value (true unless explicitly set to false). 5. Note: this only confirms the default encryption configuration. Existing objects are NOT re-encrypted. To verify existing objects, use S3 Inventory or check individual objects with HeadObject. 6. If verification fails: check for competing automation, SCPs that restrict PutBucketEncryption, or bucket policies that enforce a different encryption.

Specification.ExpectedEndState: The S3 bucket has SSE-KMS configured as the default encryption. All new objects uploaded without explicit encryption headers will be encrypted with the specified KMS key (or the AWS managed aws/s3 key). S3 Bucket Keys are enabled to reduce KMS API costs. Every object decrypt operation generates a CloudTrail event for audit purposes. The KMS key policy controls which principals can access the encrypted data. Existing objects retain their original encryption — they are NOT re-encrypted by this change.

Examples.AwsCli:
# SNAPSHOT
aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket amzn-s3-demo-bucket 2>/dev/null || echo 'No encryption configuration'

# Verify KMS key exists (if using CMK)
aws kms describe-key --key-id ${KmsKeyId} --query 'KeyMetadata.{KeyId:KeyId,Enabled:Enabled,KeyState:KeyState}'

# FIX: Set default encryption to SSE-KMS with Bucket Keys
aws s3api put-bucket-encryption --bucket amzn-s3-demo-bucket \
  --server-side-encryption-configuration '{
    "Rules": [{
      "ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {
        "SSEAlgorithm": "aws:kms",
        "KMSMasterKeyID": "'${KmsKeyId}'"
      },
      "BucketKeyEnabled": true
    }]
  }'

# If using AWS managed key (omit KMSMasterKeyID):
# aws s3api put-bucket-encryption --bucket amzn-s3-demo-bucket \
#   --server-side-encryption-configuration '{
#     "Rules": [{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {"SSEAlgorithm": "aws:kms"}, "BucketKeyEnabled": true}]
#   }'

# VERIFY
aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket amzn-s3-demo-bucket \
  --query 'ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration.Rules[0].{Algorithm:ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault.SSEAlgorithm,KeyId:ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault.KMSMasterKeyID,BucketKey:BucketKeyEnabled}'
# Expected: Algorithm=aws:kms, KeyId=<your-key>, BucketKey=true

# ROLLBACK (security regression):
# aws s3api put-bucket-encryption --bucket amzn-s3-demo-bucket \
#   --server-side-encryption-configuration '{"Rules": [{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault": {"SSEAlgorithm": "AES256"}, "BucketKeyEnabled": false}]}'
Examples.CloudFormation:
Resources:
  EncryptedBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Ref BucketName
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: 'aws:kms'
              KMSMasterKeyID: !Ref KmsKeyArn  # Omit for AWS managed key
            BucketKeyEnabled: true

  # KMS key (if using CMK):
  EncryptionKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    Properties:
      Description: KMS key for S3 bucket encryption
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableRootAccountAccess
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:aws:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'

Parameters:
  BucketName:
    Type: String
  KmsKeyArn:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: KMS key ARN (leave empty for AWS managed key)

TraitTitles: The S3 bucket is not encrypted at-rest with AWS KMS keys
